claims.claim: Samsung Health Data SDK is an Android interface to selected records in the Samsung Health app data store, including Energy Score and specified health record types.
claims.evidence: Samsung lists the SDK's exact read and write data types, requires Samsung Health 6.30.2 or later and describes access to selected app data rather than a cloud account API.

claims.claim: A distributed Samsung Health Data SDK application requires Samsung partnership approval and production registration.
claims.evidence: Samsung says unapproved applications work only with developer mode enabled and requires a partnership request before distribution.

claims.claim: Samsung Health Data SDK developer mode is for testing or debugging and is not an ordinary end-user deployment route.
claims.evidence: The guide says developer mode is ONLY for testing/debugging, while registered partner apps are matched by package name, release signature and allowed data scopes.

claims.claim: Samsung Health SDK for Android was deprecated on 31 July 2025 and Samsung directs developers to Samsung Health Data SDK.
claims.evidence: The current legacy overview contains the dated deprecation notice and replacement link.

claims.claim: Samsung Health synchronizes selected record types with Health Connect in both directions after user authorization.
claims.evidence: Samsung documents writes from Samsung Health to Health Connect, reads back into Samsung Health, separate permissions and an explicit type mapping.

claims.claim: Samsung Health activity-tracker data are not synchronized with Health Connect under Samsung's published mapping.
claims.evidence: Samsung explicitly distinguishes exercise tracker mappings from the activity tracker and states that activity-tracker data are not synchronized.

claims.claim: Health Connect requires an additional history permission for an app to read other apps' records older than the default 30-day window.
claims.evidence: Google's current read guide documents a default 30-day window and PERMISSION_READ_HEALTH_DATA_HISTORY for older records.

claims.claim: Samsung Health Sensor SDK exposes raw accelerometer, ECG and PPG plus selected processed Galaxy Watch measurements.
claims.evidence: The current SDK overview names raw accelerometer/ECG/PPG and processed heart rate, body composition, oxygen, skin temperature and other trackers.

claims.claim: A distributed Samsung Health Sensor SDK watch application requires Samsung partner approval and registration.
claims.evidence: Samsung says an unregistered Sensor SDK app works only with developer mode and requires a partner request before distribution.

claims.claim: Samsung Health Accessory SDK is an approved inbound BLE-device integration rather than a consumer data extraction route.
claims.evidence: Samsung describes verified BLE devices synchronizing glucose, pressure, heart rate, weight, cycling and exercise data into Samsung Health.

claims.claim: Samsung Health Research Stack is open-source study infrastructure for participant collection, surveys, portals and backend APIs, not a Samsung Health account API.
claims.evidence: Samsung describes participant onboarding/consent, surveys, a study portal and backend data engine built around Android and Wear OS study apps.

claims.claim: Samsung Health app/device features include outputs that are not present in the current Data SDK read-type list.
claims.evidence: The app page documents medications, cycle tracking, regional health records, AGEs and coaching, while the Data SDK's explicit read list omits several of those families.

claims.claim: Current Samsung Health personal downloads are machine-readable, but no current first-party versioned archive schema or completeness guarantee was found.
claims.evidence: Samsung's former export answer now redirects to this generic support page; current local parsers independently observe CSV, JSON and binary attachments, so exact archive parity remains a hands-on gap.

claims.claim: Strava currently maintains a Samsung Health connection article, but exact transferred fields and historical behavior require rendered or hands-on revalidation.
claims.evidence: The live Strava help-center article was modified in August 2026, but automated extraction exposes its title/metadata rather than a durable field-level payload table.

claims.claim: Samsung's current developer catalogue does not document a general public cloud API for arbitrary Samsung Health consumer accounts.
claims.evidence: Current Samsung surfaces are on-device Data/Sensor/Accessory SDKs, Health Connect and study infrastructure; no consumer account REST or GraphQL endpoint is documented.

claims.claim: v-2841/samsung-health-export parses a downloaded Samsung Health folder into self-describing JSON with a per-datatype coverage manifest.
claims.evidence: The repository documents the in-app download workflow, CSV/JSON input, zero-dependency Python output and MIT licence.

claims.claim: Devasy/samsung-health-sdk parses Samsung export CSV, JSON and attachment directories into data frames and reports.
claims.evidence: The repository documents supported export structures, parsing APIs, current 2026 development and an MIT licence.
